snippet.title: Ranthambore Travel Guide 2025 | Jungle Safari, Luxury Stay & Things to Do in 2 Days
snippet.description:
Planning a trip to Ranthambore? In this complete Ranthambore travel guide, we share everything you need to know for a 2–3 day road trip from Delhi NCR or Gurgaon to Ranthambore National Park. Thanks to the new Delhi–Mumbai Expressway, you can now reach Ranthambore in just 4 hours from Gurgaon, making it a perfect weekend getaway.

We stayed at the luxurious Aamaghati Wildlife Resort, just minutes from the safari gates, where we experienced a mix of comfort, Rajasthani culture, and wellness with the Sri Sri Spa. In this vlog, we take you through:

Ranthambore Jungle Safari – spotting tigers, deer, and wildlife in core zones
Things to do in Ranthambore – visiting Ranthambore Fort, Trinetra Ganesh Temple, Dastkar Ranthambore, Ranthambore School of Art, Rajiv Gandhi Museum of Natural History, Kala Gaura Temple & Chauth Mata Temple
Food & Culture – enjoying Rajasthani food, folk dance performances, and shopping local crafts.

This vlog is your complete Ranthambore itinerary – combining adventure, history, spirituality, and luxury stay. Whether you’re visiting for tiger safari or a peaceful family vacation, this video will help you plan the perfect trip.

Best time to visit Ranthambore: October to March (but tiger sightings are amazing in summer too!)
Nearest station: Sawai Madhopur | Nearest airport: Jaipur
Watch till the end for our travel tips, food highlights, and full Ranthambore experience.

snippet.title: Delhi Wala Radio : देशभर में बारिश और बाढ़ ने तबाही मचाई... | Flood News | New GST Rates List
snippet.description:
Delhi Wala Radio : देशभर में बारिश और बाढ़ ने तबाही मचाई... | Flood News | New GST Rates List

दिल्ली वाला रेडियो टीवी रोजाना सुबह 8: 55 मिनट पर ZEE Delhi NCR And Haryana पर Live....

#Delhi #DelhiWalaRadio  #ZEEDNH 

GST काउंसिल की बैठक में बड़ा फैसला लिया गया... अब सिर्फ 2 GST स्लैब 5% और 18% होंगे... वित्त मंत्री सीतारमण ने बताया कि दूध, रोटी, पिज्जा ब्रेड, छेना समेत कई फूड आइटम GST फ्री होंगे... इंडिविजुअल हेल्थ और लाइफ इंश्योरेंस पर भी टैक्स नहीं लगेगा। 33 जीवन रक्षक दवाएं, दुर्लभ बीमारियों और गंभीर बीमारियों के लिए दवाएं भी टैक्स फ्री होंगी... हालांकि लग्जरी आइटम्स और तंबाकू प्रोडक्ट्स पर 40% GST लगाया जाएगा... वित्त मंत्री ने बताया कि नए स्लैब नवरात्रि के पहले दिन यानी 22 सितंबर से लागू हो जाएंगे.


दिल्ली में भारी बारिस के बाद जाम की स्थिति है.. यमुना नदी के बढ़ते जलस्तर को देखते हुए, मजनू का टीला से सलीमगढ़ बाईपास तक आउटर रिंग रोड पर यातायात बुरी तरह प्रभावित है। वज़ीराबाद-सिग्नेचर ब्रिज और चंदगी राम अखाड़ा-आईपी कॉलेज रेड लाइट से यातायात डायवर्जन लागू रहेगा।

यात्रियों को सलाह दी जाती है कि वे इन मार्गों से बचें, वैकल्पिक मार्गों का उपयोग करें, सड़क किनारे पार्किंग से बचें और सुचारू आवागमन के लिए यातायात कर्मियों के निर्देशों का पालन करें।

कश्मीरी गेट रिंग रोड पर यमुना बाढ़ का पानी आने से ट्रैफिक बहुत धीमी गति से चल रहा है। मजनू का टीला की ओर जाने वाली रोड पर ट्रैफिक की गति बहुत धीमी है, पुलिस भी तैनात है। सिविल लाइन की ओर जाना चाहेंगे तो अंदर के रास्ते को बंद कर दिया है। उस रास्ते पर पानी भर रखा है।


There is a traffic jam situation in Delhi after heavy rains.. In view of the rising water level of Yamuna river, traffic on Outer Ring Road from Majnu Ka Tila to Salimgarh Bypass is badly affected. Traffic diversion will be in place from Wazirabad-Signature Bridge and Chandgi Ram Akhara-IP College Red Light.

Commuters are advised to avoid these routes, use alternate routes, avoid roadside parking and follow the instructions of traffic personnel for smooth traffic.

Traffic is moving very slowly due to Yamuna flood water on Kashmiri Gate Ring Road. Traffic speed is very slow on the road going towards Majnu Ka Tila, police is also deployed. If you want to go towards Civil Line, the inner road has been closed. That road is filled with water.


About Channel:
ज़ी दिल्ली एनसीआर हरियाणा रीज़न का सबसे भरोसेमंद हिंदी न्यूज़ चैनल है। जो 24 घंटे लगातार देश और प्रदेश से जुड़ी हर ब्रेकिंग न्यूज़, न्यूज़ अपडेट, राजनीति, मनोरंजन और खेल से जुड़ी तमाम खबरें आपके लिए लेकर आता है। इसलिए सब्सक्राइब करें और बने रहें ज़ी दिल्ली एनसीआर हरियाणा के साथ |

snippet.title: Narela Food Tour Part 2 Delhi Street Food | Spicy Tikki, Creamy Malai Chaap & Momos | Veggie Paaji
snippet.description:
Join Veggie Paaji for Part 2 of our Narela Food Tour, where we dive into Delhi's best evening street food! In this episode, we explore the bustling streets of Narela to bring you the most delicious and iconic snacks. From the legendary crispy tikki and refreshing Dahi Bhalle to creamy Malai Chaap and spicy momos, this video is a treat for every food lover.
We visit:
• Suraj Tikki Mashoor & Dahi Bhalle Bhandar: Serving incredible crispy tikki with tangy chutneys and refreshing Dahi Bhalle.
• PDM Chaap Point: A local favorite for their perfectly grilled Malai Chaap and Afghani Chaap, available in rolls.
• The Momos House: For authentic and spicy steamed momos that will set your tastebuds tingling.
Narela is a hidden gem for street food, and Veggie Paaji is here to uncover all its culinary delights. Don't forget to like, share, and subscribe for more amazing food adventures!

snippet.title: Old MANALI Food Tour l Sabali + Lazy Dog + Dylan’s + Corner House + Chopstick + Chha Meat + Kukkad
snippet.description:
We went on an Old Manali food tour with our host, Khushboo Barry, an entrepreneur who also runs a homestay in the valley. Manali, with its snow-draped peaks, pine-covered slopes, and the Beas River rushing through, has long been a travelers’ haven. Beyond the views and mountain air, the food scene here is equally fascinating, shaped by locals, long-term settlers, and visitors from around the world who have made it their home.

Our first stop was Sabali Bakery, started by a Sudanese man and his wife. Over the years it has grown into one of the most happening spots in Old Manali, especially popular with the young international crowd. The menu is colorful, eclectic, and full of energy. We tried a refreshing chia pudding, a soft bagel with cream cheese, and a delicate matcha tart, each reflecting the café’s global spirit.

From there we walked to Dylan’s Coffee House, an iconic name in Old Manali. The café has a loyal following of travelers who return again and again for its cozy atmosphere and irresistible bakes. We had the chance to meet one of the founders, who shared their journey of starting the café and nurturing it into the landmark it is today. Their legendary secret cookies lived up to the reputation, and the strong bulletproof coffee gave us just the right kick to carry on with our day.

Next on the trail was The Lazy Dog Café, where we were welcomed by its owner, once a TV journalist, who traded the newsroom for the warmth of hospitality. He shared stories of how the café took shape along the banks of the river. The food here was exceptional—perfectly cooked rainbow trout fish, a fresh smoked chicken salad, and sushi rolls that brought a touch of Japanese finesse to the mountains.

The Cornerhouse Restaurant and Café was our next stop, run by Siddharth, a young entrepreneur and trained chef. His menu reflects both his culinary skills and his love for experimenting with flavors. We sampled the beetroot carpaccio, fried chicken wings, lamb burger, and pan-seared trout fish, each dish crafted with attention to detail. Paired with some Belgian ale, it made for a truly satisfying meal.

To balance all this modern flair, we then visited Chopsticks, one of the oldest and most reliable places in Manali. Known for hearty Tibetan fare, this stop was all about comfort. A steaming bowl of mixed gyathuk, with its broth rich in flavor and noodles perfectly cooked, was just the kind of soulful food one craves in the mountains.

We couldn’t resist a sweet detour at Jeet Sweet Shop, an old-style mithai shop tucked into the town. Walking in felt like stepping back in time, with trays lined with traditional sweets that have been part of Manali’s food culture for generations. We tasted their khoye ki burfi, dal ki burfi, nariyal ki burfi, along with besan ki burfi, crispy namak pare, and sev buniya. Each bite carried the charm of recipes that haven’t changed in decades.

The food tour came to a fitting close at Kachnar Restaurant, where we were served a curated Himachali meal. The spread included chha gosht, a mutton curry cooked in yogurt-based gravy, and Himachali kukkad curry, both paired with hot tandoori rotis. The meal ended on a sweet note with meetha bhat, a fragrant sweet rice dish. 
This journey through Old Manali’s cafés and kitchens was more than just about food, it was about the people, their stories, and the way flavors from around the world have found a home in this mountain town.

Next on the trail was The Lazy Dog Café, where we were welcomed by its owner, once a TV journalist, who traded the newsroom for the warmth of hospitality. He shared stories of how the café took shape along the banks of the river. The food here was exceptional—perfectly cooked rainbow trout fish, a fresh smoked chicken salad, and sushi rolls that brought a touch of Japanese finesse to the mountains.

The Cornerhouse Restaurant and Café was our next stop, run by Siddharth, a young entrepreneur and trained chef. His menu reflects both his culinary skills and his love for experimenting with flavors. We sampled the beetroot carpaccio, fried chicken wings, lamb burger, and pan-seared trout fish, each dish crafted with attention to detail. Paired with some Belgian ale, it made for a truly satisfying meal.

To balance all this modern flair, we then visited Chopsticks, one of the oldest and most reliable places in Manali. Known for hearty Tibetan fare, this stop was all about comfort. A steaming bowl of mixed gyathuk, with its broth rich in flavor and noodles perfectly cooked, was just the kind of soulful food one craves in the mountains.

We couldn’t resist a sweet detour at Jeet Sweet Shop, an old-style mithai shop tucked into the town. Walking in felt like stepping back in time, with trays lined with traditional sweets that have been part of Manali’s food culture for generations. We tasted their khoye ki burfi, dal ki burfi, nariyal ki burfi, along with besan ki burfi, crispy namak pare, and sev buniya. Each bite carried the charm of recipes that haven’t changed in decades.

The food tour came to a fitting close at Kachnar Restaurant, where we were served a curated Himachali meal. The spread included chha gosht, a mutton curry cooked in yogurt-based gravy, and Himachali kukkad curry, both paired with hot tandoori rotis. The meal ended on a sweet note with meetha bhat, a fragrant sweet rice dish. 
This journey through Old Manali’s cafés and kitchens was more than just about food, it was about the people, their stories, and the way flavors from around the world have found a home in this mountain town.

snippet.title: पुरानी दिल्ली के मशहूर छोले कुलचे | Chole Old Delhi style | Instant Gajar Achaar | Chef Ranveer Brar
snippet.description:
PURANI DILLI CHOLE - Weekend ka matlab something special for the whole family. What better than this Old Dilli style Chole Kulche 😋😋

***********************
𝗔𝗠𝗔𝗭🥘𝗡  𝗦𝗛🍳𝗣
🛒RB Store - https://www.amazon.in/shop/chefranveer
📟Kitchen Appliances - https://bit.ly/KitchenAppliancesIUse
🔪Knives I use - https://amzn.to/4kzSJVe

***********************
𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗰𝗸 𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗼𝗼:
Tari wale Chane
Instant Chole - 
***********************

PURANI DILLI CHOLE

Preparation time 15 minutes
Cooking time 25-30 minutes
Serve 2-4 

Ingredients
For Cooking Chole
500 gms Chickpeas (soaked overnight) भीगे हुए छोले
½ tsp Turmeric powder, हल्दी पाउडर
2-3 no. Garlic cloves (optional) लहसुन
Prepared bouquet garni, मसालों की पोटली
Water as required, पानी
3 tbsp Ghee, घी
Salt to taste, नमक स्वादअनुसार
3-4 tbsp Tamarind pulp, इमली का पानी
1 tsp Jaggery, गुड़
4 heaped tbsp Prepared masala, तैयार किया हुआ मसाला
1 tsp Black peppercorns, crushed, कुटी हुई काली मिर्च
½ cup Chickpeas water, छोले का पानी
Prepared tira, तैयार किया हुआ तीरा
2 tbsp fresh Coriander leaves, chopped, धनिया पत्ता

For Bouquet garni
3 no. Black cardamom, बड़ी इलायची
2 tsp Black peppercorns, काली मिर्च के दाने
1 tbsp Tea leaves, चायपत्ती
3-4 no. Cloves, लौंग
4 no. dry Kashmiri red chillies, सूखी कश्मीरी लाल मिर्च

For Masala
3 tbsp Coriander seeds, धनिये के बीज
½ tbsp Cumin seeds, जीरा
3-4 tbsp Black peppercorns, काली मिर्च के दाने
7 no. Black cardamom, बड़ी इलायची
8-10 no. Green cardamom, हरी इलायची
4-5 no. Cloves, लौंग
1 tsp Fennel seeds (optional) सौंफ़
Salt to taste, नमक स्वादअनुसार

For Gajar Mirch Ka Achaar
1 cup Water, पानी
2 medium Carrots (peeled & cut into batons) गाजर
2 no. Green chillies (less spicy & roughly chopped) हरी मिर्च
Salt to taste, नमक स्वादअनुसार
1 heaped tbsp Vinegar, सिरका
2 tbsp Jaggery, गुड़
1 tsp Degi red chili powder, देगी लाल मिर्च पाउडर
¼ tsp Turmeric powder, हल्दी पाउडर
½ tsp Coriander powder, धनिया पाउडर
1 tsp dry Mango powder, आमचूर पाउडर

For Ginger Green Chilli Paste
4 inch Ginger (peeled & chopped) अदरक
5 no. Green chillies (less spicy & roughly chopped) हरी मिर्च

 For Tira
3-4 tbsp Oil, तेल
2-3 tbsp Ghee, घी
1 tsp Cumin seeds, जीरा
Prepared Ginger Green chilli paste, अदरक हरी मिर्च का पेस्ट
A pinch of asafoetida, हींग
2 heaped tbsp Degi red chili powder, देगी लाल मिर्च पाउडर
200 ml Ghee, घी

For Searing Kulcha
1 tsp Ghee, घी
2 no. Kulcha, कुलचा
1 tbsp Prepared tira, तैयार किया हुआ तीरा

Other Ingredients
3-4 tbsp Red tamarind (soaked for 1hr) भीगी हुई लाल इमली

For Garnish
Coriander sprig, धनिया पत्ता
Green chilli, slit into half,  हरी मिर्च
Lemon wedge, नींबू की फांक

Process 
For Cooking Chole
● In a pressure cooker, add soaked chickpeas, turmeric powder, garlic, prepared bouquet garni, water as required, ghee and mix well.
● Cook it for 3-4 whistles until cooked well.
● Open the lid, add salt to taste, tamarind pulp, jaggery, prepared masala, crushed black peppercorns, chickpeas water and let it simmer for 10-12 minutes until thickens.
● Finish it with prepared tira and fresh coriander leaves.
● Transfer it to a serving dish, garnish it with coriander sprig, green chilli and lemon wedge.
● Serve hot with seared kulcha.

For Bouquet Garni
● Take a small piece of muslin cloth, add black cardamom, black peppercorns, tea leaves, cloves, dry kashmiri red chillies and make a potli of it.
● Keep it aside for further use.

For Masala
● In a pan, add coriander seeds, cumin seeds, black peppercorns, black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves, fennel seeds, salt to taste and dry roast them until it's aromatic.
● Transfer it to a mixer grinder jar and grind it into fine powder.
● Keep it aside for further use. 

For Gajar Mirch Ka Achar
● In a pan, add water, carrots, green chilli and let boil it for 7-8 minutes.
● Add vinegar, jaggery, degi red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, dry mango powder and simmer for 4-5 minutes.
● Transfer it to a bowl or cleaned jar and keep it aside for further use.

For Ginger Green Chilli Paste
● In a mortar pestle, add ginger, green chillies and grind it into coarse paste.
● Keep it aside for further use.

For Tira
● In a handi, add oil, ghee, once it's hot, add prepared ginger garlic paste, a pinch of asafoetida and cook it for 2-3 minutes.
● Add degi red chili powder and cook for a minute on low flames.
● Finish it with ghee and let it cook for a while.
● Turn off the flames and keep it aside for further use.

For Searing Kulcha
● In a pan, add ghee, once it's hot, place kulchas, pour some prepared tira and sear the kulchas on both the sides until it's golden in colour.
● Transfer it to a serving dish and serve hot with prepared chole.

Preparation time 15 minutes

4 heaped tbsp Prepared masala, तैयार किया हुआ मसाला
1 tsp Black peppercorns, crushed, कुटी हुई काली मिर्च
½ cup Chickpeas water, छोले का पानी
Prepared tira, तैयार किया हुआ तीरा
2 tbsp fresh Coriander leaves, chopped, धनिया पत्ता

For Bouquet garni
3 no. Black cardamom, बड़ी इलायची
2 tsp Black peppercorns, काली मिर्च के दाने
1 tbsp Tea leaves, चायपत्ती
3-4 no. Cloves, लौंग
4 no. dry Kashmiri red chillies, सूखी कश्मीरी लाल मिर्च

For Masala
3 tbsp Coriander seeds, धनिये के बीज
½ tbsp Cumin seeds, जीरा
3-4 tbsp Black peppercorns, काली मिर्च के दाने
7 no. Black cardamom, बड़ी इलायची
8-10 no. Green cardamom, हरी इलायची
4-5 no. Cloves, लौंग
1 tsp Fennel seeds (optional) सौंफ़
Salt to taste, नमक स्वादअनुसार

For Gajar Mirch Ka Achaar
1 cup Water, पानी
2 medium Carrots (peeled & cut into batons) गाजर
2 no. Green chillies (less spicy & roughly chopped) हरी मिर्च
Salt to taste, नमक स्वादअनुसार
1 heaped tbsp Vinegar, सिरका
2 tbsp Jaggery, गुड़
1 tsp Degi red chili powder, देगी लाल मिर्च पाउडर
¼ tsp Turmeric powder, हल्दी पाउडर
½ tsp Coriander powder, धनिया पाउडर
1 tsp dry Mango powder, आमचूर पाउडर

For Ginger Green Chilli Paste
4 inch Ginger (peeled & chopped) अदरक
5 no. Green chillies (less spicy & roughly chopped) हरी मिर्च

 For Tira
3-4 tbsp Oil, तेल
2-3 tbsp Ghee, घी
1 tsp Cumin seeds, जीरा
Prepared Ginger Green chilli paste, अदरक हरी मिर्च का पेस्ट
A pinch of asafoetida, हींग
2 heaped tbsp Degi red chili powder, देगी लाल मिर्च पाउडर
200 ml Ghee, घी

For Searing Kulcha
1 tsp Ghee, घी
2 no. Kulcha, कुलचा
1 tbsp Prepared tira, तैयार किया हुआ तीरा

Other Ingredients
3-4 tbsp Red tamarind (soaked for 1hr) भीगी हुई लाल इमली

For Garnish
Coriander sprig, धनिया पत्ता
Green chilli, slit into half,  हरी मिर्च
Lemon wedge, नींबू की फांक

Process 
For Cooking Chole
● In a pressure cooker, add soaked chickpeas, turmeric powder, garlic, prepared bouquet garni, water as required, ghee and mix well.
● Cook it for 3-4 whistles until cooked well.
● Open the lid, add salt to taste, tamarind pulp, jaggery, prepared masala, crushed black peppercorns, chickpeas water and let it simmer for 10-12 minutes until thickens.
● Finish it with prepared tira and fresh coriander leaves.
● Transfer it to a serving dish, garnish it with coriander sprig, green chilli and lemon wedge.
● Serve hot with seared kulcha.

For Bouquet Garni
● Take a small piece of muslin cloth, add black cardamom, black peppercorns, tea leaves, cloves, dry kashmiri red chillies and make a potli of it.
● Keep it aside for further use.

For Masala
● In a pan, add coriander seeds, cumin seeds, black peppercorns, black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves, fennel seeds, salt to taste and dry roast them until it's aromatic.
● Transfer it to a mixer grinder jar and grind it into fine powder.
● Keep it aside for further use. 

For Gajar Mirch Ka Achar
● In a pan, add water, carrots, green chilli and let boil it for 7-8 minutes.
● Add vinegar, jaggery, degi red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, dry mango powder and simmer for 4-5 minutes.
● Transfer it to a bowl or cleaned jar and keep it aside for further use.

For Ginger Green Chilli Paste
● In a mortar pestle, add ginger, green chillies and grind it into coarse paste.
● Keep it aside for further use.

For Tira
● In a handi, add oil, ghee, once it's hot, add prepared ginger garlic paste, a pinch of asafoetida and cook it for 2-3 minutes.
● Add degi red chili powder and cook for a minute on low flames.
● Finish it with ghee and let it cook for a while.
● Turn off the flames and keep it aside for further use.

For Searing Kulcha
● In a pan, add ghee, once it's hot, place kulchas, pour some prepared tira and sear the kulchas on both the sides until it's golden in colour.
● Transfer it to a serving dish and serve hot with prepared chole.
